brand_names: Check with your pharmacist for the exact brand name available in your country
what_its_for: This combination medicine is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It contains three medicines that work together in different ways to lower your blood pressure and reduce the risk of heart attack, stroke, and kidney problems. Telmisartan blocks a hormone that tightens blood vessels, amlodipine relaxes and widens blood vessels, and indapamide helps your kidneys remove extra salt and water from your body.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth, exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with a glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Try to take it at the same time every day — many people find it easiest to take in the morning. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet unless your doctor or pharmacist tells you it is safe to do so.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your blood pressure and how you respond to treatment. A common starting approach is one tablet once daily. Do not change your dose on your own. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions on the prescription label.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is already the next day or almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom or near the kitchen sink. Keep this medicine in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and cause dizziness or fainting. Do not use potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium without asking your doctor first. Avoid getting up too quickly from sitting or lying down, especially in the morning, as this medicine can cause dizziness. Avoid prolonged exposure to heat or dehydration (such as heavy sweating, vomiting, or diarrhea) without staying well hydrated. Tell your doctor or dentist about this medicine before any surgery or dental procedure.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: swelling of your face, lips, throat, or tongue (signs of a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); chest pain or irregular heartbeat; sudden severe dizziness, fainting, or feeling very lightheaded; significant swelling in your legs or ankles; muscle cramps, weakness, or unusual tiredness (possible signs of low potassium); decreased urination or signs of kidney problems; yellowing of your skin or eyes; or if your blood pressure readings remain very high despite taking your medicine. Also call your doctor if you become pregnant while taking this medicine.
when_it_works: You may start to see a reduction in your blood pressure within 1 to 2 weeks of starting treatment. However, it may take 4 to 6 weeks to feel the full benefit of this medication. It is very important to keep taking it every day even if you feel well, because high blood pressure often has no symptoms. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Telmisartan and indapamide can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby, especially during the second and third trimesters. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine and tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if all components pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to dizziness and low blood pressure effects. Rise slowly from sitting or lying positions to reduce fall risk. Kidney or liver disease: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely. Children: This medicine is generally not recommended for children. Always tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as many drugs can interact with this combination.
